source_title: One Piece Creator Oda Cancels New Arc Permanently
source_excerpt:
One Piece creator Eiichiro Oda is known for his meticulous story writing and tremendous world-building. His magnum opus, One Piece , has continued for almost 30 years now, and this series is getting better with each passing year. The franchise has gotten so big that it has also received its own live-action adaptation by Netflix, which, interestingly enough, the creator of the series is also heavily involved in.
Recently, Steve Maeda, one of the showrunners of Netflix's One Piece live-action, confirmed that Eiichiro Oda was directly involved in the cancellation of an arc, which would have taken the live-action series on a completely different path from the manga and the anime, making it non-canon. This new arc would've completely changed the character as well as the introduction of Usopp, and would have led to significant changes to the Syrup Village arc as well. Thankfully, Eiichiro Oda completely cancelled it and, alongside it, made other significant changes to the first season of the series.
Eiichiro Oda Officially Cancelled New Live-Action-Exclusive Arc Focused On Usopp As Syrup Village Replacement
One Piece's East Blue Saga is incredibly important, as it sets the basis for Luffy and the Straw Hat Pirates before their adventure in the Grand Line. In the live-action, this journey of the Straw Hat Pirates, while not fully faithful to the manga, covers all the main important arcs . However, Steve Maeda, the showrunner of the first season of the series, revealed that Netflix initially had very different plans for the East Blue Saga. Specifically, Netflix wanted to make significant changes to the character of Usopp, as well as the famous arc of Syrup Village, where Luffy and the Straw Hats go on to recruit him to the crew.
According to Steve Maeda, the initial plan for Netflix was to reduce the overall episode count of the live-action series to 8 episodes instead of 10. Having 10 episodes gave Netflix's One Piece live-action enough time to cover every arc in the East Blue Saga properly. However, 8 episodes would have posed a significant challenge for the series and would have led to some major cuts in terms of story arcs.
Steve Maeda revealed that the biggest change came with Usopp's arc. As we know, Usopp's arc is Syrup Village, where Luffy goes on to recruit him, and they fight against Captain Kuro and the Black Cat Pirates. Initially, Netflix wanted Usopp's introduction to be on Gaimon's Island instead of Syrup Village, completely removing the Syrup Village arc as a process and changing Usopp's introduction to Luffy, as well as his induction into the Straw Hat Pirates.
This change to One Piece live action could have affected the canon of the story drastically. It would have removed the characters of Kaya as well as the Usopp Pirates. It would also have removed the likes of Captain Kuro and affected the Strawhat acquisition of the Going Merry. Most importantly, it would have utterly destroyed Usopp's characterization and removed one of the biggest arcs from the series. Furthermore, in return, it would have given us a completely new arc, which not many fans would have cared about in the grand scheme of things. Thankfully, Eiichiro Oda was not in favor of doing this new live-action arc based on Gaimon's Island and instead decided to protest against it, leading to its cancellation.
Why Oda Cancelled Netflix's New One Piece Live Action Arc
The primary reason why Eiichiro Oda wanted this new Gaimon-based arc cancelled in One Piece live action was simply that he wanted the series to be faithful to the original manga. When Eiichiro Oda gave his project to Netflix, who were at the time looking to create a live-action series for the brilliant story following Monkey D. Luffy, the condition was to bring to life the very story that Oda told. Naturally, there are going to be deviations from the manga , but Oda strictly wanted the series to follow the canon pathway. This is precisely why Oda completely rejected these changes, simply telling Netflix that this wasn't what he had agreed to.
Upon Oda's protests and complaints, Netflix reportedly decided to change their stance towards the first season of the live action and go all in. Instead of 8 episodes, the total episode count was pushed back to 10. At the same time, the budget for Netflix live action was increased drastically, allowing for 2 more episodes to be produced. Finally, Syrup Village was reincorporated into the story once again, with Gaimon's arc being completely removed as a result.
This change may seem small in the grand scheme of things, but it completely led to the cancellation of a Gaimon-based arc, which would have changed Usopp's character significantly and, most importantly, taken away one of the most beautiful arcs in the entirety of the East Blue saga in the form of Syrup Village. It is also interesting to note that the Syrup Village adaptation of the One Piece live action was incredibly fun. While not as intense as Arlong Park, it had its fun moments, and it would have been a missed opportunity not to include it in the final product. Thankfully, Oda's protests saved the day.

As has been confirmed to us on various occasions, Eiichiro Oda is closely working with Netflix to ensure that the live-action series does not stray from the promises made to the creator when a deal was struck between them long ago. To that end, Eiichiro Oda even takes a lot of trips to Cape Town in South Africa, where filming for the live-action series often takes place. Oda recently flew to Cape Town for One Piece live-action Season 3 as it wrapped up filming for the Arabasta Saga . Similarly, Oda will continue to work closely with the live-action crew as it now heads into the Skypiea arc of the series.
With Oda working so closely with the live-action staff, it goes without saying that the series is going to be incredibly exciting moving forward, and we are all waiting to see how it brings the world of One Piece to life in an even better manner. As things stand, One Piece live-action Season 3 is set to be released in 2027 , in the summer. This new live-action season is going to finally wrap up the Arabasta Saga and push the Straw Hat Pirates towards the adventure in the Sky Islands, which is one of the most chaotic and adventurous parts of the entire series. Given that Oda is going to be working closely with Netflix on this new project, the series is going to get even better, and we absolutely cannot wait for the show to come to life once again.
One Piece Live Action is available to stream with two seasons on Netflix .
